chapter: Starting out in New York and Chicago
title: Alvin Burroughs and the battle with Chick Webb at the Chicago Savoy
summary: Drummer Alvin 'Mouse' Burroughs came from Earl Hines' band; in a battle of bands before 5,000 people against Chick Webb and Ella Fitzgerald, Horace says his band won.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Getting the thing over to -- and here's another guy in my band that I had. Unfortunately, he died young. His name was Alvin Burroughs. We called him Mouse. Tom, he was one of the greatest drummers. In fact, I

had the pleasure of playing the Savoy Ballroom in Chicago in the thirties and Chick Webb, along with Ella Fitzgerald, the great Ella Fitzgerald, during the years 'A Tisket, A Tasket' was a popular tune.
We played a battle of music at the Savoy Ballroom. We had 5,000 people in that ballroom with this particular band against Chick Webb. I hate to say it, but we won.

When I say we won, as great a drummer as the Camel we called Chick Webb was, Alvin Burroughs played so much drums that night, Chick Webb's guys didn't get off the stand, and let this guy take a solo. God bless him, he died young, but he's got a young son in Chicago, they tell me, that plays just like him. I've never been fortunate enough to go back to hear him.

He was a terrific drummer. He was -- I got him -- he was with Earl Hines, and those guys came over to my band, you know, they didn't wanna -- Earl Hines went on the road quite a bit, you know, and they didn't want to travel. They were family guys, you know. I was fortunate enough to
stay at Swingland, you know, I was broadcasting on WBBM out of Chicago, but I had a great band there.
